items.title: A man found in Tennessee in 1991 has his name back
body: On April 10, 1991, a man's remains were found in a neighborhood in McMinn County, Tennessee. For more than 30 years, no one knew who he was.

On Nov. 19, 2026, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) and the McMinn County Sheriff's Office named him: Forest Wayne Loudermilk, originally from North Carolina. His family last saw him around 1980.
In 2025, the TBI sent a sample to Othram, a DNA lab in Texas. Othram's tests pointed to possible relatives. Then a relative's DNA confirmed who he was.
items.help: Did you know Forest Wayne Loudermilk? Detectives want to hear from you, and they are looking for any photo of him. Call the McMinn County Sheriff's Office at 423-745-5620, ext. 1928.
items.note: The sources do not say how he died.
items.sourceNote: All three reports come from one TBI announcement.
items.next: Detectives are now trying to learn what happened to him before he died.

items.kind: A cold case moves to court
items.title: A 2007 Queens cold case moves to court
body: Martha Vega was found dead in her home in Ridgewood, Queens, on Sept. 10, 2007.

Blood was left at the scene. In 2022, Othram, a DNA lab, turned it into a profile that could be used for family-tree DNA searches. The Queens District Attorney's Cold Case Unit then built the family tree.

Prosecutors say that work led to Javier Segarra. He was arrested in South Carolina on Nov. 4, 2026. On Nov. 24, he was arraigned in Queens on a charge of second-degree murder, and a judge ordered him held in jail. His next court date is Jan. 15, 2027.
items.status: He is charged, not convicted, and he is presumed innocent. The sources we read do not say how he pleaded.
items.quote: For almost two decades, Martha Vega's murder went unsolved, but she was never forgotten.
